items.title: Rent tax breaks set for December 1
items.body: Royal Decree-law 29/2026 has been published, with changes due December 1; parliamentary validation remains pending. Landlords cutting rent by more than 5% could get up to 100% relief on net rental income under IRPF (personal income tax), subject to conditions. Eligible tenants could request one- or two-year extensions.

items.title: Cabinet approves 5.3% minimum wage rise
items.body: Cabinet approved a 5.3% rise in the SMI (minimum wage) to €18,004 a year from January 2027. An IRPF (personal income tax) deduction of €1,033.58 would remove tax at that wage, fading out at €23,172 income. The tax decree still needs parliamentary validation before November 29. Minimum-wage earners would also have no monthly withholding.

items.title: Court suspension affects 113,326 Ley de Nietos voters
items.body: A precautionary Supreme Court suspension prevents 113,326 citizens naturalised under the Ley de Nietos from voting on November 29 because they have not proven descent from exiles. The party Iustitia Europa will ask the court to check compliance and clarify other electoral records.

items.title: Cabinet approves 4.5% public sector pay rise
items.body: Cabinet approved a Royal Decree-law for a 4.5% pay rise in 2027 covering more than three million public employees. Central administration staff will get the increase in their January 2027 payroll.

items.title: Brussels raises growth forecast as inflation persists
items.body: The European Commission forecasts Spanish growth of 2.6% in 2026 and 2.1% in 2027, helped by AI-related exports and a resilient labour market. It expects average CPI (consumer price index) inflation of 3.9% in 2026 as disruption in the Strait of Hormuz distorts oil and gas markets. Higher interest rates are making borrowing costlier.

items.title: Home sales fall as protected housing shrinks
items.body: September home sales fell 13.4% year on year to 54,548 amid high prices and limited supply. Protected housing's share of sales fell from 10.25% in 2016 to 6.39% in January–September 2026. Few new protected developments and homes losing protected status help explain that decline.

items.title: Ryanair plans €500 million Seville engine centre
items.body: Ryanair plans to invest €500 million in its first European engine maintenance centre in Seville, creating 600 skilled jobs. The 28,000 m² site is due to start operating in mid-2029. The airline will also open an engineering academy in the city.

items.title: Election programmes split over pension inflation guarantees
items.body: PP, PSOE, and Frente Amplio pledge to keep pensions rising with CPI (consumer price index); Vox's programme makes no such pledge. PSOE and Frente Amplio also propose a constitutional guarantee. That would require two-thirds of Parliament, far beyond the support polls suggest.

items.title: Spain seeks Frontex rule changes for Canaries
items.body: Spain is asking the EU to change Frontex rules to enable ships and aircraft to patrol off Senegal and Gambia. A formal deployment request has not been made, and Senegal's consent would be needed. The push follows 12,121 irregular arrivals on the Canary Islands route so far in November.

items.title: PP proposes 20% tax for incoming tech workers
items.body: The PP's election programme proposes a 20% tax rate for six years for workers moving to Spain for large tech projects. Modelled on the Beckham Law, it would also target Spaniards returning from abroad. The proposal is not law; the programme also promises personal AI training cheques for workers.

items.title: Election rivals debate on November 19
items.body: PSOE candidate Pedro Sánchez and PP candidate Alberto Núñez Feijóo face each other on November 19 at 22:00 in a two-hour televised debate. Housing, taxes, public services, corruption, and migration are on the agenda. RTVE, Atresmedia, Mediaset, and regional channels will broadcast it before the November 29 election.

items.title: Raising a child now costs €835 monthly
items.body: Raising a child in Spain costs an average €835 a month, up 2.7% from 2024, Save the Children reports. Housing is the biggest driver, with housing and food accounting for almost half the total. About 847,000 households with children lack enough income to cover the cost.
